---
title: "How do I plot two numeric variables with a trend line and point labels?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I plot two numeric variables with a trend line and point labels?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Check every x has a corresponding y.

2. Plot labeled axes and individual points.

3. Overlay lm() and label an observation only when useful.

## Runnable example

```{r}
snow_cm <- c(10,15,20,25,30,40)
visitors <- c(85,91,110,125,139,168)
plot(snow_cm,visitors,type="n",xlab="Snow depth (cm)",
     ylab="Visitors",main="Illustrative paired measurements")
grid(col="gray85")
points(snow_cm,visitors,col="#3F78A8",pch=19)
fit <- lm(visitors ~ snow_cm)
abline(fit,col="#A35E20",lwd=2,lty=2)
text(snow_cm[6],visitors[6],labels="last observation",pos=2,cex=.75)
legend("topleft",legend=c("Observations","Linear fit"),
       pch=c(19,NA),lty=c(0,2),
       col=c("#3F78A8","#A35E20"),bty="n")
```

## Interpret the result

The points show the observed pairs, while the dashed line summarizes one fitted linear trend. The line should not be used outside the observed range without a separate justification.

## Check before applying to real data

Plot paired rows only. A straight-line fit does not prove causation or rule out curved relationships.
